problem: Real-to-sim conversion for embodied AI is hard: scan-based simulators (Habitat) are uneditable and artifact-ridden, NeRF/3DGS yield uneditable representations without physics, and CAD-based methods need precise instance segmentation. Indoor occupancy prediction is also limited by scarce, noisy, low-diversity real-world datasets.
motivation: Voxel semantic occupancy aligns naturally with Minecraft blocks, so predicted occupancy can be translated directly into editable, physically grounded scenes usable for embodied tasks such as VLN. Reconstruction quality depends on occupancy accuracy, which in turn is bottlenecked by data, motivating a cheap automatic occupancy-data generation pipeline in Minecraft.
key_idea: Convert real-world RGB sequences into editable Minecraft scenes via multi-frame 3D semantic occupancy prediction, instance-center clustering and furniture-template retrieval, and use Minecraft itself (mods for PBR and block-level labels) to auto-generate a large occupancy dataset (MinecraftOcc).
insight: Occupancy-based reconstruction with shape-aware template matching beats text-layout-based scene generation (LayoutGPT, I-Design, LayoutVLM) on semantic integrity, collisions and realism (Table on layout comparison). Manual refinement is light (about 24.5 operations, 70.38s per scene versus 482s from scratch), meaning the automatic reconstruction is a good but imperfect initialization. On MinecraftOcc, existing models score low, and joint training with 8k MinecraftOcc gives a small NYUv2 gain for Symphonies (IoU +0.43, mIoU +0.21), so the dataset is both a hard benchmark and a modest complement.
method: Occupancy prediction and fusion: a pretrained EmbodiedOcc (monocular predictor plus embodied fusion using camera intrinsics and extrinsics) produces a unified scene semantic occupancy grid from an RGB sequence.
Instance center extraction: binarize the occupancy, compute a local density map via a 3D uniform-kernel convolution, and threshold at tau to get candidate object centers.
Per-class DBSCAN clustering: cluster the centers within each semantic class using an L2 threshold eta and take the centroids as distinct object instances.

Template retrieval: align each instance's occupancy with a furniture library over discrete rotations by maximizing 3D IoU, then emit Minecraft build commands (TMEO mod) and optionally refine with the SceneForge visualization/editing tool.

MinecraftVLN: room-tour trajectories in 15 reconstructed scenes plus 5 community scenes are segmented, human-annotated, and turned into Next-View and Next-Action QA tasks; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B are fine-tuned with SFT (LLaMA-Factory) or RFT (EasyR1, GRPO), and Gemini-2.5-Pro is used as a live controller.

MinecraftOcc pipeline: the Screen with Coordinates mod captures screenshots and poses (intrinsics from FOV, extrinsics from yaw/pitch); a fixed volume is placed by axis-aligned or diagonal yaw case; a viewpoint-aware fallback offset and frustum culling refine it; WorldEdit queries block types as voxel labels (1,452 classes, mapped to 12/13 classes for evaluation).

setting.backbone: EmbodiedOcc (pretrained, for reconstruction); Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B (SFT/RFT fine-tuned) for VLN; Gemini-2.5-Pro (frozen) for the live navigation demo
setting.training_data: EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet for occupancy; MinecraftVLN (Base 1,059 / Extend 2,483 samples; up to 1000 training samples for SFT); MinecraftOcc (8k/50k/100k images) for occupancy benchmarks; NYUv2 for mixed training
setting.observation: first-person RGB sequences with camera intrinsics/extrinsics (occupancy); egocentric RGB views in Minecraft for VLN
setting.action_space: Next-Action: discrete high-level actions (move forward, turn left, etc.); Next-View: image prediction; Gemini controller issues step-wise Minecraft actions
setting.simulator: Minecraft (with WorldEdit, Screen with Coordinates, TMEO mods, PBR shaders)
setting.privileged: Reconstruction uses camera poses; for MinecraftOcc GT labels come from Minecraft map data; 15-30 scenes were manually refined

numbers.extra: trained on MinecraftOcc 8k; benchmark baseline, not a proposed method

numbers_note: VLN table reports fractions as accuracy (converted to 0-100). Gemini-2.5-Pro navigation is only shown qualitatively. Layout-comparison and efficiency tables are not standard benchmarks and are omitted.
results: Reconstructed scenes are visually consistent with real ones; fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL reaches up to 80.0% Next-Action and about 67.5% Next-View accuracy (vs. zero-shot 3B/7B far lower, e.g. 19-39%). Existing occupancy models score low on MinecraftOcc (best mIoU ~21.6), and mixing 8k MinecraftOcc into NYUv2 training lifts Symphonies to 50.34 IoU / 29.91 mIoU. The pipeline beats layout-based baselines on semantic integrity (0.913) and realism (6.145), and cuts scene refinement time about 7x versus building from scratch.
limitations: Automatic reconstruction is suboptimal, so manual refinement is needed (30 scenes refined, 15 used for VLN), and the reconstruction is limited to the retrieval library plus a blocky Minecraft rendering.

VLN evaluation is small (3.8k samples), lacks standard navigation metrics (SR/SPL) and closed-loop quantitative results (Gemini demo is only qualitative); the reported numbers do not compare with standard VLN methods.
The gain from MinecraftOcc on NYUv2 is marginal (+0.43 IoU, +0.21 mIoU) and sim-to-real generalization is not thoroughly validated.
